column4: RECOIL has no DCX. First page of the DCX offset table decoded with the PCX decoder; first page matches Deark (dcx module, then its PCX decoder) and, for the files Pillow can read, Pillow's DCX reader. Three fax pages store x_max one pixel past their 216-byte rows (1729 wide): output is 1728 wide, equal to Deark's PNG without its extra column (which is the next row's first pixel). Output reviewed: fax text, black on white.

RECOIL rejects DGI (Digi-Pic; its .dgi is the Atari 8-bit APAC format). Layout from Deark's dgi module: four interlaced 320x200 CGA screens joined into 640x400, magic at offset 32000. Matches Deark's PNG pixel for pixel on all five files and on a sixth kept out of the corpus. Palette is Deark's choice (CGA palette 0, low intensity), a guess. Output reviewed: picture and text run across the quadrant borders without seams.

BA arrays: largest entry. Output reviewed: recognizable icons and pointers.
